statement.on_screen: nothing: no caption or key on the picture (as v7)
statement.to_be_said_elsewhere: PROPOSED LEVEL · 12.7 M · VYSHNEVSKYI & SHEVCHUK 2024 · THE PLANTS' DYING COMPRESSED FROM YEARS · THE BED'S HEIGHTS INFERRED · DRAWN; and that the view under the water, its silt and the plants' dying are drawn. Where (the shot's caption field, a card or the credits) is the user's decision.

said_so: SPECULATIVE AND DRAWN: the water, its rise, ripples, reflections and murk, the silt, the lens crossing, the view from under the surface, and now the plants' dying (their browning, leaf and twig loss, slumping, falling, settling into the bed and dissolving) and its pace. Nothing is observed and nothing is generated by an AI tool: the plants are v3's procedural models, the scene the flight south's.

TIME IS COMPRESSED FROM YEARS, NOT MONTHS: the rise is drawn in 10 s and the dying in about 12 s. As general knowledge, to be checked against a source before it is said in the film (no source was read for this shot): herbs and grasses of dry ground die within weeks under water; white willow tolerates long flooding of its roots, and permanent deep flooding kills it over one to a few growing seasons; drowned trunks often stand for years or decades in reservoirs. So the shot draws years in seconds, and the trunks' disappearance (fallen, settled into the bed, dissolved into the silt) is a drawing simplification, so the end can hold on the tower and the wires (the user's ask).

The order is a drawing of how these plants die under water, not a simulation: the herbs and grasses first (they go under first: they wilt, brown, slump and dissolve into the silt), then the reeds (brown, lean, break and fall), the shrubs and saplings, and the willows and poplars last (leaves yellow-brown and thinning, bare branches, the trunks leaning over and settling into the bed). Each plant starts when the drawn water reaches its base, in the shot's compressed time.

Plants whose ground lies above the proposed level are left alive (642 far trees on higher ground, 600 m and more off; they are not seen at the end: the view through the surface near the horizon is absorbed).
The silt settling as the dying ends (the absorption toward the bottom lengthening a little from 10.5 s to 13.5 s, the bed greyed toward silt up to 0.92) is drawn.
The level is a proposal: 12.7 m Baltic (Vyshnevskyi & Shevchuk 2024, p. 286), 13.1 m in the scene (EGM2008, Baltic +0.4 m). The bed's heights it rises through are inferred (scene3d/bed.py).

The view through the surface is a drawn convention (Snell's window not drawn; the water above the eye drawn clear enough for the tower and the lit wires to stay readable). The flow dashes are the film's drawing convention (the record's state of 11 September 2026); the far birds are v5's drawn birds.

The sound is v7's, unchanged (the same 15 s, the same lens crossing): the soundscape continued, only the synthesized line, muffled under water (drawn). The dying has no sound of its own: no sound effects.

approach.why: the plants are dense and layered: removing them per pixel against one plate without plants would also remove plants hidden behind them and never show what each dying plant uncovers. So the plants change in Blender, per frame, and the picture, the heights and the wire matte are rendered per frame; v7's compositor draws its water on them unchanged.
approach.blender: still_v8.py: v3's models and placement and v5's camera f exactly; the instancer (Geometry Nodes, Instance on Points) takes per plant a rotation (its own turn and its fall), a scale (slump), a position (settling) and four values the plant material reads as instancer attributes: dead (colour), leaf, twig and fade (losses, against one random number per leaf, blade, card or stem, and a stem's thickness order, added to the models as face attributes: the models' geometry and colours untouched). Losses are a transparency (dithered at 32 samples in the picture; a hard cut in the one-sample height pass).
approach.dieoff: dieoff_v8.py (plain numpy): each plant's start = when v7's drawn level reaches its base (at least 0.8 s, when v7 has the water fully drawn) + its kind's lag; its kind's phases; the kind's deadline (a plant reached late dies faster, down to 0.45x); fall directions random, those within 14.0 m of the eye away from it (never into the lens); per-plant jitter of lag (0.35 s) and pace (0.12).
approach.passes_per_frame: static_K.exr (the picture without the moving parts: 2x until frame 140, from above the water; 1x after, under it), pos_K.exr (heights and distances, 2x, one exact sample), matte_K.exr (the lit wires white over everything else black, 1x, every 5th frame and the last, linear between)

approach.composite: composite_v8.py: v7's composite_v7.py imported unchanged; per frame its plate, heights and matte replaced by the frame's (v5's 1080p plate plus the 2x plate's change from v6's, so unchanged pixels are v5's exactly, as in v7)

seen: 0-4.2 s (over the water): the herbs, reeds and willows turn yellow-brown and grey-brown as the water climbs them; the herbs at the waterline slump; the reed blades thin.
4.2-9 s (under): the herbs and reeds collapse and settle, the willows lose their leaves, stand bare, lean and settle; the crowns above the surface die with them, wavering through it.

From about 9.5 s the view reads clear: the last stages of the far plants (settling, dissolving) happen in the murk. The mean change between frames falls to the ripples' alone from 9 s (0.4 of 255 at a quarter size, against 2.4-6.4 while the plants fall). So the clear hold is about 5.5 s, longer than the 2-3 s aimed for: trim the shot's out to about 12.5 s, or slow the trees' pace and render again.
The bed under the water is barely seen: v7's murk and depth darkening leave it a dark floor (lengthening the absorption at the end, tried at up to 2.3x, changed little).
No flicker found: the largest step between frames is at the lens crossing (frame 124); the 2x-to-1x switch at frame 140 and the matte's 5-frame steps show no jump.
